findings.title: Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates
findings.body: The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but retrieves credentials for the requesting user and constructs EventManager for that user. When someone other than the organizer invokes this mutation, their credentials do not provide access to the organizer's referenced calendar event. Guests are already saved, but the organizer's calendar can remain unchanged or the update can fail. Initialize the calendar update with the booking organizer's credentials instead.

findings.title: Prevent guest additions from bypassing seated-event reservations
findings.body: This mutation creates attendee rows without checking seatsPerTimeSlot, remaining capacity, or creating corresponding seat-reference records. The new action is also exposed on seated bookings, and existing attendees are authorized to invoke it. Consequently, an attendee can add arbitrary guests to a fully booked slot, exceeding its configured capacity and bypassing the normal seat-management lifecycle. Either reject seated bookings or add guests through the seat-reservation flow.

findings.title: Accept either the team administrator or owner role
findings.body: The isTeamAdminOrOwner check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, requiring both checks to succeed. A team administrator without the owner role therefore receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to another host's team booking, unless they happen to be an attendee. Use || so either authorized team-management role can perform this operation.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are converted to lowercase, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. The server schema accepts uppercase email addresses, so a caller can submit BLOCKED@example.com to bypass a blacklist entry for blocked@example.com and still create and email that guest. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and storage.

findings.title: Enforce guest uniqueness on the server
findings.body: The uniqueGuests filter only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted array. The server schema also accepts duplicates, so submitting the same new email twice passes both checks and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees and notifications. The dialog's Set validation does not protect direct API calls. Deduplicate or reject duplicate addresses on the server before persisting them.

findings.title: Check booking status before issuing confirmed invitations
findings.body: There is no booking-status validation before adding guests and sending notifications. The UI exposes this action for past PENDING bookings, and cancelled or rejected bookings can also be submitted directly through tRPC. The mutation sends booking-confirmation emails to new guests and CONFIRMED iCalendar requests to existing attendees, incorrectly representing these meetings as confirmed. Restrict the operation to accepted bookings or make its notifications explicitly respect the current booking status.

findings.title: Honor disabled standard-email settings for guest additions
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept event-type metadata. Unlike the neighboring scheduling and location-change paths, it cannot honor disableStandardEmails.all.host or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest therefore sends standard emails—including scheduled emails to new guests—even when the event owner disabled them in favor of custom notifications. Pass the event metadata from the handler and apply the existing host and attendee email-disable checks.
